Definition: from G4443; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever:--be sick of a fever.
BiblicalUsage: Simon's wife's mother lay sick of a fever, and when they told Jesus about her, He came and took her by the hand and the fever left her.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this small word matters because Jesus did not preach at the fever, He touched the woman, and her healing was immediate and practical.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
